articles.titleJa: 文化庁が著作権小委員会を開催
articles.title: Agency for Cultural Affairs Holds Copyright Committee Meeting
articles.summaryJa: 文化庁は第26期文化審議会著作権分科会政策小委員会の第2回会合を11月9日に開催すると発表しました。

5級.title: Japan Has a Meeting
5級.text: The Agency for Cultural Affairs has a meeting. It is about copyright. The meeting is on November 9, 2026. People can watch it online. The government talks about important rules. Everyone can check the new news on the website.

4級.title: Agency Holds Copyright Meeting
4級.text: The Agency for Cultural Affairs announced a new meeting in Japan. It is the second meeting of the policy subcommittee. The event will take place on November 9, 2026. Officials will talk about measures against pirate sites. They plan to hear from related groups during the session. People can watch the live stream online.

3級.title: Agency Announces Second Policy Subcommittee Meeting
3級.text: The Agency for Cultural Affairs announced that it will hold its second policy subcommittee meeting. The event is scheduled for November 9, 2026. Officials will gather at the Ministry of Education and also hold an online session. They plan to hear from related groups about anti-piracy measures. People who want to watch the discussion can register for a live stream online. The agency will publish the meeting documents on its official website before the event starts for everyone to read.

準2級.title: Cultural Affairs Agency Schedules Second Copyright Subcommittee Meeting
準2級.text: The Agency for Cultural Affairs announced that it will hold the second meeting of the policy subcommittee on November 9, 2026. The session will take place at the Ministry of Education and through an online broadcast. During the meeting, members will conduct hearings with related organizations regarding anti-piracy measures. The agency plans to broadcast the proceedings live so that the public can observe the discussion. Interested individuals can register online through the provided registration forms to access the live stream before the deadline. Meeting documents will also be published on the official website.

2級.title: Agency for Cultural Affairs Schedules Copyright Policy Subcommittee Session
2級.text: The Agency for Cultural Affairs has officially announced that it will hold the second meeting of the 26th Cultural Council Copyright Division Policy Subcommittee on November 9, 2026. The session is scheduled to take place at the Ministry of Education East Building Special Conference Room, and it will also be held via an online platform. According to the announcement, the planned agenda includes conducting hearings with related organizations regarding countermeasures against copyright piracy, alongside other matters. To ensure transparency, the agency plans to publicly broadcast the proceedings through a live stream instead of allowing in-person observers. Interested participants must complete their registration using the designated online form within the established application period, which runs from November 2 until November 5, 2026. Furthermore, meeting documents will be published on the official website around 12:00 PM on the day of the event so that the public can review them prior to the start of the discussions.

準1級.title: Agency for Cultural Affairs Schedules Second Copyright Subcommittee Meeting
準1級.text: The Agency for Cultural Affairs has officially confirmed the schedule for the second meeting of the twenty-sixth Cultural Council Copyright Division Policy Subcommittee. The governmental session is scheduled to take place on November ninth, 2026, at the Ministry of Education East Building Special Conference Room, and it will also be conducted through an online broadcast option. The agenda for the subcommittee meeting will focus primarily on conducting hearings with related industrial organizations concerning comprehensive countermeasures against copyright piracy, in addition to other general matters. The government body has arranged for a public live stream of the proceedings to maintain complete transparency, replacing traditional in-person observation. Members of the general public and news media representatives are strictly mandated to complete their registration through designated digital forms prior to the established application deadline of November fifth, 2026. For news media personnel, specific guidelines permit brief on-site photography during the opening moments, provided that the media personnel register in advance and wear designated press armbands. Comprehensive meeting documentation will also be made publicly available on the official Agency for Cultural Affairs website by approximately noon on the day of the scheduled discussions for thorough public review.

articles.title: Japan Holds First AI and Digital Reform Council Meeting
articles.summaryJa: デジタル庁は、AI・デジタル改革推進会議の第1回会合を開催し、AX社会の実現に向けた論点を議論しました。

5級.title: Level 5: Simple News
5級.text: Japan has a new meeting. It is about AI and digital reform. The first meeting is in Tokyo. Ministers and experts talk here. They want to use AI in society. They want to make life better. The government will work hard on this plan.

4級.title: Level 4: Basic News
4級.text: Japan held the first meeting of the AI and Digital Reform Council at the Prime Minister's Office. Cabinet ministers and experts gathered to talk about artificial intelligence and digital reform. Officials said that Japan faces a population decline and labor shortages. They need to use AI to rebuild supply structures and realize an AX society. The council discussed key points like trustworthy AI, new rules, and social implementation in various fields to prepare for the future.

3級.title: Level 3: Intermediate News
3級.text: The Digital Agency of Japan recently published the minutes from the first meeting of the AI and Digital Reform Council. Cabinet officials and industry experts gathered at the Prime Minister's Office to discuss national technology strategies. Because Japan faces a shrinking population and labor shortages, leaders emphasized that digital reform is necessary to maintain social and economic stability. They talked about five main points, including a vision for trustworthy AI by the end of the year, updating regulations, and accelerating technology use in fields such as manufacturing and healthcare.

準2級.title: Level 2: Upper Intermediate News
準2級.text: The Digital Agency of Japan has released the official record of the inaugural AI and Digital Reform Council meeting held at the Prime Minister's Office. Chaired by key cabinet officials, the council brought together academic experts and business leaders to discuss national technology strategies. Officials highlighted that Japan faces severe structural labor shortages driven by a declining population. To maintain economic stability, the government aims to drive artificial intelligence and digital transformation forward. The discussion focused on establishing a clear vision for trustworthy AI by the end of the year, updating regulatory frameworks, accelerating social implementation in labor-deficient sectors, strengthening AI governance against risks, and improving foundational environments.

2級.title: Level 1: Advanced News
2級.text: The Digital Agency of Japan has officially published the minutes and associated documents from the inaugural meeting of the AI and Digital Reform Council, which took place at the Prime Minister's Office. Convened by high-ranking cabinet ministers alongside distinguished academics and industry executives, the council addressed the critical imperative of integrating artificial intelligence into the nation's socio-economic fabric. In the face of a declining population and structural labor shortages, leaders argued that maintaining traditional economic frameworks is no longer viable. Consequently, the administration is prioritizing growth and crisis-management investments powered by digital innovation. The session centered on five core deliberation topics: formulating a comprehensive vision for trustworthy AI applications by year's end to update the artificial intelligence basic plan, reforming regulations in cooperation with regulatory panels, accelerating social implementation across labor-intensive sectors such as manufacturing and healthcare, reinforcing institutional governance to mitigate emerging risks like advanced cyber threats, and upgrading cross-cutting environments encompassing data, systems, and human resources.

準1級.title: Level S: Professional News
準1級.text: The Digital Agency of Japan has officially published the minutes and associated documents from the inaugural meeting of the AI and Digital Reform Council. Convened at the Prime Minister's Office and co-chaired by high-ranking cabinet ministers alongside distinguished academics and industry executives, the council addressed the critical imperative of integrating artificial intelligence into the nation's socio-economic fabric. In the face of a rapidly aging demographic and structural labor shortages, leaders argued that maintaining traditional economic frameworks is no longer viable. Consequently, the administration is prioritizing robust growth and crisis-management investments powered by digital innovation. The session centered on five core deliberation topics: formulating a comprehensive vision for trustworthy AI applications by year's end to update the artificial intelligence basic plan; reforming regulations and establishing new principles in cooperation with regulatory panels; accelerating social implementation across labor-intensive sectors such as manufacturing and healthcare; reinforcing institutional governance to mitigate emerging risks including advanced cyber threats; and upgrading cross-cutting environments encompassing data, systems, and human resources. Ministers emphasized leveraging unique domestic data assets, particularly in disaster management and industrial automation, to transform demographic challenges into global technological advantages.

articles.titleJa: 広島のかき水揚げ開始
articles.title: Hiroshima Oysters Harvest Begins
articles.summaryJa: 昨年大量死の被害を受けた広島特産の養殖かきが、例年より約1か月遅れて11月2日に水揚げを始めました。関係者には期待と不安の両方があります。

5級.title: Oysters Start
5級.text: Hiroshima oysters can start now. Last year, many oysters died here. Today, fishermen start to take them out of the water. People are happy. But some people feel worried. This is a big news for Japan today.

4級.title: Hiroshima Oysters Harvest Begins
4級.text: Famous oysters from Hiroshima can be harvested today. Last year, many oysters died in the sea. This year, the work starts about one month later than normal years. Local people have high hopes for the new season. However, they also have some worries about the harvest. People in Hiroshima want to see good results this time. Fishermen are working hard today.

3級.title: Hiroshima Oysters Harvested Today
3級.text: Famous farmed oysters in Hiroshima have started their harvest season today. Last year, a large number of these oysters died unexpectedly in the water. Because of that damage, the harvest began about one month later than usual. Local workers feel very happy to start their work again. At the same time, many people still feel worried about the new season and the future of their business.

準2級.title: Hiroshima Oysters Start Season
準2級.text: Farmed oysters, which are a famous specialty of Hiroshima, finally started their seasonal harvest today, coming about one month later than in typical years. This follows a serious disaster last year when a massive number of farmed oysters died unexpectedly in the water. Because of those past damages and difficulties, local people involved in the industry feel a complex mix of strong hope and deep anxiety as the new fishing season begins. Workers and business owners hope that everything goes well this year and that they can recover from the losses of the previous season, while keeping a close watch on the situation.

2級.title: Hiroshima Oyster Harvest Begins with Hope and Worry
2級.text: Farmed oysters, which are a major specialty product of Hiroshima, officially began their seasonal harvest today, starting approximately one month later than in a typical year. This delayed opening comes after last year when the region suffered severe damage, with a massive number of farmed oysters dying unexpectedly in the water. Due to those lingering concerns from the previous disaster, today's resumption of work brings out mixed emotions across the local community. While industry workers and related personnel are filled with anticipation to finally resume their operations and bring their products to market, many voices continue to express deep anxiety about what this new season will actually bring for their business. Furthermore, local people are closely watching how the oysters will grow this season after the heavy losses experienced last year, hoping that the industry can recover steadily over the coming months as operations continue across the region.

準1級.title: Hiroshima Oyster Harvest Starts Late Amid Mixed Feelings of Hope and Anxiety
準1級.text: Farmed oysters, which represent a cherished and famous specialty product of Hiroshima Prefecture, officially commenced their seasonal harvesting operations today on November second, arriving approximately one month later than the usual schedule in a typical year. This delayed start follows a devastating period last year when the local aquaculture industry suffered catastrophic losses, as a massive number of farmed oysters perished unexpectedly in the water due to severe environmental pressures such as decreasing oxygen concentration levels. As local workers and industry participants finally pull the first batches from the sea today, people connected to the industry express a complex combination of eager anticipation and profound anxiety. They desperately hope for a stable and prosperous season to help rebuild their livelihoods, yet the painful memories of last year's severe damage leave many watching the current situation very carefully to see how the harvest develops over the coming weeks and months. Industry participants, fishermen, and local observers note that while everyone is glad to see the new season finally get underway across Hiroshima Prefecture, uncertainty remains a major factor for everyone involved in producing and distributing these famous regional products throughout the broader market. Furthermore, the local community and related organizations continue to monitor the water conditions and the growth of the surviving oysters very closely, hoping that the industry can recover steadily after the unprecedented difficulties and heavy losses experienced during the previous season.

articles.titleJa: アイルランド代表の挑戦
articles.title: How Ireland are shaping up for the Nations Championship
articles.summaryJa: アイルランド代表は秋の国際大会に向けて準備を進めており、強豪相手に巻き返しを図ります。

5級.title: アイルランドのラグビー
5級.text: Ireland has a good rugby team. Andy Farrell is the coach. They play games in autumn. They want to win. Argentina and Fiji are playing soon. South Africa is also coming to Dublin. Ireland can play very well. Fans are happy to watch them.

4級.title: アイルランドの秋の試合
4級.text: Ireland is preparing for the Nations Championship. Andy Farrell is the coach of the team. They will play against Argentina, Fiji, and South Africa in Dublin this month. In the past, Ireland had some difficult losses to top teams. Now, they want to win and show their best skills. The team is working hard to improve every game and make fans happy.

3級.title: アイルランド代表の新しい挑戦
3級.text: As Ireland prepares for the 2026 Nations Championship, coach Andy Farrell is shaping up his side. They will face Argentina, Fiji, and South Africa in Dublin over the next three weeks. Ireland wants to improve after some tough losses against top teams like New Zealand and France. Winning against the world champions, South Africa, would be a huge statement for the team and help them build confidence for the future.

準2級.title: アイルランド代表の巻き返しに向けた挑戦
準2級.text: As Ireland prepares for the 2026 Nations Championship, coach Andy Farrell is shaping up his squad for a crucial autumn series. Over the next three weeks, Ireland will host Argentina, Fiji, and South Africa in Dublin. The team aims to improve its trajectory following a series of difficult defeats against rugby heavyweights, including New Zealand and France. Although Ireland showed brilliant form against England earlier this year, recent losses have raised questions about their standing among elite teams. Facing the world champion Springboks will be a major test for Farrell's conditioned side, especially after prop Tadhg Furlong was confirmed available for selection following a disciplinary review.

2級.title: ネイションズ・チャンピオンシップへ向けたアイルランド代表の状況
2級.text: As Ireland prepares for the autumn series in the 2026 Nations Championship, Andy Farrell's side is shaping up for a demanding schedule. The team faces upcoming matches against Argentina, Fiji, and South Africa in Dublin over the next three weeks. While Ireland previously reached the top of the world rankings, recent years have brought persistent defeats against rugby heavyweights like New Zealand, France, and South Africa. Ireland has lost their past six meetings with these elite teams by double-digit margins. Despite a thrilling victory over England earlier this year, Farrell's side needs a strong performance this month to alter their narrative. Defeating world champions South Africa, who won 24-13 on their last visit to Dublin, would provide a vital boost on the journey to the next World Cup. To strengthen their squad, Ireland has placed a heavy emphasis on physical conditioning, while the availability of seasoned prop Tadhg Furlong provides a timely lift for the front row.

準1級.title: アイルランド代表が迎える試練の秋：ネイションズ・チャンピオンシップへの展望
準1級.text: As Ireland prepares for the northern hemisphere series in the 2026 Nations Championship, attention turns to how Andy Farrell's side is shaping up for a demanding autumn schedule. With Argentina, Fiji, and South Africa set to visit Dublin over the coming weeks, Ireland faces a crucial opportunity to recalibrate its trajectory. The context surrounding the team has shifted notably since the previous World Cup cycle, during which Ireland peaked at the summit of the world rankings following an iconic series victory over the All Blacks in New Zealand. However, subsequent defeats against rugby's traditional heavyweights—including New Zealand, France, and South Africa—have prompted questions regarding the squad's standing among the global elite. Ireland has suffered six consecutive losses to these top-tier opponents by double-digit margins, with heavy reversals against France and New Zealand highlighting persistent vulnerabilities. Although these setbacks are tempered by a brilliant performance against England earlier in the year, Farrell's men must extinguish error-prone tendencies to avoid unprecedented home defeats against Argentina and Fiji. The ultimate test will arrive when they renew hostilities with world champions South Africa, whose formidable scrum dismantled the Irish pack in a previous Dublin encounter. In their pursuit of redemption, the coaching staff has placed an intensified focus on conditioning as a distinct competitive advantage, while the confirmation of Tadhg Furlong's availability offers a timely boost for the front row as they prepare to battle the world champions.

articles.titleJa: 厚生労働省が戦没者慰霊事業
articles.title: MHLW Announces November 2026 Memorial Projects
articles.summaryJa: 厚生労働省は令和8年11月に実施する戦没者慰霊事業および遺骨収集の計画を発表しました。

5級.title: Japan Has Memorial Projects
5級.text: Japan has new memorial projects. They start in November 2026. The Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare makes this plan. People go to Iwo Jima and other places. They look for bones of fallen soldiers. Ministry workers and members join this important work.

4級.title: Japan Announces Memorial Projects for November
4級.text: Japan announced memorial projects for November 2026. The Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare leads this important work. Teams will visit places like Papua New Guinea, Iwo Jima, and the Solomon Islands. They collect remains of fallen soldiers. Bereaved families can also join memorial pilgrimages to honor them. Ministry officials and authorized association members work together on these missions.

3級.title: Ministry Announces November Memorial and Bone Collection Plans
3級.text: The Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare in Japan has announced its memorial projects for November 2026. These activities include collecting remains and memorial pilgrimages in several regions. Teams will travel to Eastern New Guinea, the Solomon Islands, Iwo Jima, and the Philippines. Ministry officials and members of an authorized association will work together on these missions. Families will also visit Iwo Jima and the Philippines to pay their respects and remember the fallen soldiers.

準2級.title: Japan Outlines Government Memorial and Bone Collection Projects for November
準2級.text: The Japanese Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare has released its schedule for memorial projects and remains collection slated for November 2026. These missions are designed to recover the remains of fallen soldiers and offer memorial pilgrimages for bereaved families. Teams consisting of ministry officials and members of the Japan Association for Recovery and Repatriation of War Casualties will visit multiple regions. These areas include Eastern New Guinea, the Solomon Islands, Iwo Jima, and the Philippines. In addition to bone collection, grieving families will travel to Iwo Jima and the Philippines to honor their ancestors and remember those who lost their lives during the war.

2級.title: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare Details November 2026 Memorial and Recovery Operations
2級.text: The Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare of Japan has officially announced its comprehensive schedule of memorial projects and remains collection activities for November 2026. Under the Act on the Promotion of Recovery and Repatriation of War Casualties' Remains, authorized associations work closely with ministry officials to execute these vital missions. Throughout November, multiple teams will deploy to overseas locations and domestic sites, including Eastern New Guinea in Papua New Guinea, the Solomon Islands, Iwo Jima, and the Philippines. These missions involve careful field surveys and bone collection operations to bring fallen soldiers home. Furthermore, organized memorial pilgrimages will enable hundreds of bereaved family members and ministry staff to visit Iwo Jima and the Philippines, ensuring that the memory of the fallen is honored with profound respect and dedicated government support.

準1級.title: Japan Releases Comprehensive November Schedule for War Memorial and Remains Recovery Missions
準1級.text: The Japanese Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare has officially published its detailed schedule outlining war memorial initiatives and remains recovery operations scheduled throughout November 2026. Operating under the legal framework established by the Act on the Promotion of Recovery and Repatriation of War Casualties' Remains, these national projects are carried out by the Japan Association for Recovery and Repatriation of War Casualties under strict government supervision and guidance. The November itinerary encompasses multiple distinct phases of field surveys and bone collection missions across designated foreign and domestic territories, including the fourth and fifth Eastern New Guinea field surveys and bone collection missions in Papua New Guinea, the third Iwo Jima remains recovery operation, and the Solomon Islands mission. Personnel comprising ministry officials and association specialists will coordinate these sensitive recovery efforts across all targeted regions. In parallel with the bone collection operations, government-backed memorial pilgrimages are organized for Iwo Jima and the Philippines. These pilgrimages enable scores of bereaved family members, accompanied and supported by ministry personnel, to travel to these historic sites to pay their respects and honor the memory of those who perished during the conflict. Through these carefully planned operations, the ministry continues its ongoing commitment to recovering fallen soldiers and supporting grieving families.

articles.title: Sapporo City Inspects North Safari Sapporo After Deadline Passes
articles.summaryJa: 札幌市にある動物園ノースサファリサッポロの違法建築問題で、撤去期限を過ぎても建物や動物が残っているため、札幌市が現地調査を行いました。

5級.title: Sapporo City Checks Zoo
5級.text: Sapporo City has a problem. North Safari Sapporo is a zoo. Some buildings are illegal. The city told the zoo to remove them. The time limit passed. But some buildings and animals are still there. The city checks the zoo today.

4級.title: Sapporo City Inspects North Safari Sapporo
4級.text: Sapporo City visited North Safari Sapporo today. This zoo has a big illegal building problem. The city gave an official order to remove all the buildings completely. However, the deadline has already passed. Because of this, some buildings and animals are still on the site. Therefore, city officials went to check the actual situation closely today.

3級.title: Sapporo City Conducts On-Site Inspection at Zoo
3級.text: Sapporo City conducted an on-site inspection at North Safari Sapporo today. The zoo had a serious problem involving illegally constructed buildings. The city previously issued an order to remove all the buildings by a specific date. However, that deadline has already passed, and some buildings and animals still remain at the location. Because of this situation, city officials visited the zoo to check the current status closely.

準2級.title: Sapporo City Inspects Zoo Over Unremoved Buildings
準2級.text: Sapporo City conducted an on-site inspection at North Safari Sapporo today to check its current status regarding illegal structures. The zoo had faced major issues because buildings were constructed illegally on its grounds. Although the city previously issued an official removal order requiring the complete elimination of all structures, the deadline has already passed. Despite this strict administrative order, some buildings and animals still remain at the facility because the removal could not be finished in time. Consequently, municipal officials visited the zoo today to confirm the details and address the ongoing situation directly.

2級.title: Sapporo City Inspects North Safari Sapporo After Removal Deadline Passes
2級.text: On November 2, Sapporo City conducted an on-site inspection at North Safari Sapporo, a zoo located within the city, to check its current status regarding illegal structures. This action was taken because the facility had been constructed illegally, and the deadline for an official removal order issued by the city had already passed. Despite this established deadline, some buildings and animals still remained on the premises without being completely cleared away. As a result, municipal officials visited the location to check the actual conditions directly and determine the next steps regarding the unremoved structures and animals that are still present at the site. Sapporo City previously ordered the complete removal of all structures because the zoo buildings were constructed illegally within the municipality. However, the deadline for this official removal order has now passed, and the complete removal has not been finished yet by the management of North Safari Sapporo. Because some buildings and animals still remain on the premises, municipal officials from Sapporo City visited North Safari Sapporo on November 2 to confirm the exact situation firsthand.

準1級.title: Sapporo City Officials Conduct On-Site Inspection at North Safari Sapporo Following Expiration of Building Removal Order
準1級.text: On November 2, municipal officials from Sapporo City conducted an on-site inspection at North Safari Sapporo, a local zoo situated within the municipality, to assess the current situation accurately. The inspection was prompted by an ongoing controversy regarding illegally constructed facilities at the location. Previously, Sapporo City had issued a strict removal order demanding the complete demolition of all unauthorized structures by a specified deadline. However, that official deadline has now passed, and multiple buildings along with various animals still remain on the premises of North Safari Sapporo because the necessary removal work could not be finished in time. To verify the facts firsthand and determine how to proceed with the unresolved removal issue, municipal authorities from Sapporo City visited the site today to evaluate all remaining concerns. The zoo, known as North Safari Sapporo, faced this administrative action because unauthorized buildings were erected on its grounds. Sapporo City previously ordered the complete removal of all structures because those zoo buildings were constructed illegally within the municipality. However, the deadline for this official removal order has now passed, and the complete removal has not been finished yet by the management of North Safari Sapporo. Because some buildings and animals still remain on the premises, municipal officials from Sapporo City visited North Safari Sapporo on November 2 to confirm the exact situation firsthand.

articles.titleJa: 高校生が地域ギフト制作
articles.title: High School Students Create a Local Gift Catalog
articles.summaryJa: 愛媛県の宇和高校と野村高校の生徒26人が、西予市の事業者を取材して地域産品を紹介するカタログギフトを制作しました。生徒は商品の調査、取材、撮影、記事の編集まで担当し、文化祭とオンラインで販売を始めました。

sources.name: 毎日キレイ（愛媛新聞社）

5級.title: A Gift from Our Town
5級.text: Students make a gift catalog. They visit local shops. They take photos and write about local food. They sell the catalog at school and online. The project helps people learn about their town.

4級.title: Students Share Local Products
4級.text: Students from two high schools in Ehime made a gift catalog. They visited local businesses in Seiyo City and learned about their products. The students took photos and wrote short stories. They started selling the catalog at a school festival and online.

3級.title: A Catalog Made by High School Students
3級.text: Twenty-six students from Uwa and Nomura high schools worked together on a gift catalog. They visited local businesses in Seiyo City, took photos, and wrote about products. They also learned how to edit their stories. The catalog went on sale at a school festival and online on October 31.

準2級.title: Students Connect Their Town with Shoppers
準2級.text: High school students in Ehime created a catalog gift featuring products from local businesses. Twenty-six students from Uwa and Nomura high schools researched the products, interviewed business owners, took photographs, and edited the descriptions. The project gives the businesses another way to reach customers and lets students practice communication and marketing.

2級.title: A Student-Made Catalog Promotes Ehime Businesses
2級.text: Twenty-six students from Uwa and Nomura high schools in Ehime worked with local businesses to create a catalog gift. They researched products, interviewed business owners in Seiyo City, photographed the items, and wrote and edited the introductions with help from professionals. Sales began at the Nomura High School festival and online on October 31. Part of the proceeds will support educational activities at the two schools.

準1級.title: High School Students Turn Local Reporting into a Gift Product
準1級.text: A group of 26 students from Uwa and Nomura high schools in Ehime produced a catalog gift to introduce businesses and products from Seiyo City. The students handled research, interviews, photography, writing, and editing, with guidance from professional writers, photographers, and designers. The catalog launched at the Nomura High School festival on October 31 and is also available online. Part of the proceeds will fund educational activities, while the project aims to raise awareness of local businesses and expand their reach.

articles.titleJa: 高校生が地元商品を開発
articles.title: Students and Local Businesses Make Festival Food
articles.summaryJa: 熊本県山鹿市の城北高校の生徒が地元企業と弁当やドーナツなどを開発し、学園祭で販売しました。売上は熊本地震の被災地支援に寄付されます。

5級.title: Food for a School Festival
5級.text: Students make lunch boxes and doughnuts. They work with local companies. They sell the food at their school festival. The money will help people after an earthquake.

4級.title: A Local Food Project
4級.text: Students at Johoku High School in Kumamoto worked with local companies. Together they made lunch boxes and doughnuts. Students sold the new foods at their school festival. They will give the money to help people affected by the Kumamoto earthquake.

3級.title: Students Create Festival Foods with Local Companies
3級.text: First-year students in the sports science course at Johoku High School made original food with local businesses. Their products included lunch boxes and doughnuts. They sold them at the school festival on October 30 and 31. The profits will be donated to support areas affected by the Kumamoto earthquake.

準2級.title: A School Festival Supports Local Businesses and Communities
準2級.text: Students at Johoku High School in Yamaga City worked with local companies to develop foods such as lunch boxes and doughnuts. They sold the products at their school festival on October 30 and 31. The project gave students experience in planning and selling products, and the profits will support communities affected by the 2016 Kumamoto earthquake.

2級.title: Students Put Their Ideas on the Festival Menu
2級.text: First-year students in Johoku High School’s sports science course teamed up with businesses in Yamaga City to create original lunch boxes, doughnuts, and other foods. They sold the products at the school festival over two days. The project connected classroom learning with local business, and the proceeds are expected to be donated to support areas affected by the Kumamoto earthquake.

準1級.title: Local Collaboration Brings Student-Designed Foods to a School Festival
準1級.text: Students in the sports science course at Johoku High School in Kumamoto Prefecture worked with local businesses to develop original foods, including lunch boxes and doughnuts. The products were sold at the school festival on October 30 and 31. By taking part in product development and sales, students gained practical experience, while proceeds from the project will be donated to communities affected by the Kumamoto earthquake.

articles.titleJa: 高校生×セブン伝統野菜
articles.title: Students and Seven-Eleven Bring Local Vegetables to Stores
articles.summaryJa: 甲府商業高校の生徒が生産者やセブン‐イレブン・ジャパンと連携し、山梨県の伝統野菜「長禅寺菜」を使った商品3品を開発しました。11月2日から山梨・長野の店舗で販売し、3日には高校生が学校行事で販売します。

5級.title: A Local Vegetable in Stores
5級.text: Students make new food with a local vegetable. They work with farmers and Seven-Eleven. The food goes on sale on November 2. Students will also sell it at school.

4級.title: Students Make Products with Local Farmers
4級.text: Students at Kofu Commercial High School worked with local farmers and Seven-Eleven Japan. They made three products using a traditional vegetable from Yamanashi. The products will go on sale in stores on November 2.

3級.title: A Traditional Vegetable Gets a New Look
3級.text: Students at Kofu Commercial High School helped create three products using Chozenji-na, a traditional vegetable from Yamanashi. They worked with local growers and Seven-Eleven Japan. The products will be sold in stores in Yamanashi and Nagano from November 2. Students will also sell them at a school event.

準2級.title: Students Take a Local Vegetable to Convenience Stores
準2級.text: Kofu Commercial High School students teamed up with local growers and Seven-Eleven Japan to develop three products using Chozenji-na, a traditional vegetable from Yamanashi. Sales are scheduled to begin at stores in Yamanashi and some stores in Nagano on November 2. Students will sell the products themselves at their school’s Koshō Department Store event on November 3.

2級.title: A Student Idea Reaches Convenience Store Shelves
2級.text: Students at Kofu Commercial High School worked with growers and Seven-Eleven Japan to turn Chozenji-na, a traditional Yamanashi vegetable, into three new products. The items are scheduled to go on sale in Yamanashi and at some stores in Nagano on November 2. The following day, students will sell them at their school’s annual Koshō Department Store event. The project aims to introduce the vegetable to more shoppers and support local producers.

準1級.title: Local Produce Meets Student Ideas and Retail Experience
準1級.text: Kofu Commercial High School students collaborated with local producers and Seven-Eleven Japan to develop three products featuring Chozenji-na, a traditional vegetable from Yamanashi. The products are scheduled to reach stores in Yamanashi and some locations in Nagano on November 2. Students will also sell them at the school’s Koshō Department Store event on November 3. The partnership links local agriculture with retail and gives students hands-on experience in product development and sales.

articles.title: Murata Plans to Expand Production of Tiny Electronic Parts
articles.summaryJa: 村田製作所は、スマートフォンや電子機器に使われる積層セラミックコンデンサの生産能力を今後拡大する方針を公表しました。小型化が進む電子部品の需要に応えるため、製造体制を強化します。

5級.title: A Company Makes More Parts
5級.text: Murata makes tiny parts for electronics. The company plans to make more of them. These parts are used in phones and other devices.

4級.title: Murata Plans to Make More Parts
4級.text: Japanese electronics company Murata plans to increase production of tiny parts called ceramic capacitors. Many phones and other electronic devices use these parts.

3級.title: More Tiny Parts for Electronic Devices
3級.text: Murata Manufacturing announced plans to expand production capacity for multilayer ceramic capacitors. These small components are used in smartphones and many other electronic products. The company plans to strengthen its production system to meet demand.

準2級.title: Murata Responds to Demand for Electronic Components
準2級.text: Murata Manufacturing plans to expand its production capacity for multilayer ceramic capacitors, or MLCCs. These tiny components help electronic devices store and manage electrical energy. They are used in smartphones and many other products, so stable supply is important for manufacturers.

2級.title: A Production Expansion for Components Inside Phones
2級.text: Murata Manufacturing announced plans to increase its production capacity for multilayer ceramic capacitors. MLCCs are small components found in smartphones, computers, and other electronics. Expanding capacity can help the company respond to demand as devices become more advanced and manufacturers need reliable supplies.

準1級.title: Murata Strengthens Manufacturing Capacity for Ceramic Capacitors
準1級.text: Murata Manufacturing plans to expand production capacity for multilayer ceramic capacitors, components used in smartphones and a wide range of electronic equipment. The parts are small but essential to the operation of modern devices. The company’s announced plan is intended to strengthen its manufacturing system and respond to future demand from electronics makers.

5級.title: A Festival for Farm Students
5級.text: Students from farm high schools sell food they grow. They bring crops and food to Tokyo. A restaurant also serves rice grown by students.

4級.title: High School Farm Products in Tokyo
4級.text: Yanmar held a festival with 42 agricultural high schools. Students sold crops and food they made. A restaurant in Tokyo also serves a special meal with rice grown by high school students.

3級.title: Students Sell Their Farm Products
3級.text: Yanmar held a two-day harvest festival in Tokyo on October 31 and November 1. Students from 42 agricultural high schools sold crops and processed foods they had grown or made. A restaurant also began offering a special menu using rice grown by students.

準2級.title: A Company Helps Agricultural Students Meet Customers
準2級.text: Yanmar organized a harvest festival in Tokyo with students from 42 agricultural high schools. The students sold crops and processed foods themselves, learning about selling and distribution. A restaurant at Yanmar Tokyo also began serving a limited-time course featuring rice grown by high school students.

2級.title: Agricultural Students Bring Their Work to a Tokyo Market
2級.text: Students from 42 agricultural high schools took part in Yanmar’s harvest festival in Tokyo on October 31 and November 1. They sold crops and processed foods they had grown or made, gaining experience in distribution and sales. A restaurant in the Yanmar Tokyo building also introduced a limited-time menu featuring rice cultivated by students.

準1級.title: Yanmar Event Connects Agricultural Schools with Consumers
準1級.text: Yanmar Holdings hosted a harvest festival in Tokyo featuring students from 42 agricultural high schools. The students sold crops and processed goods, giving them practical experience in how agricultural products reach customers. The company also arranged a restaurant collaboration: from November 1 through November 28, a Tokyo restaurant planned to serve a limited-time course using rice grown by high school students.

articles.title: Bird Flu Test is Negative in Miyagi
articles.summaryJa: 環境省は宮城県栗原市で回収されたマガンの死亡野鳥について、遺伝子検査の結果、高病原性鳥インフルエンザウイルスは検出されなかったと発表しました。

5級.title: Dead Bird Test is Safe
5級.text: A dead bird was found in Miyagi. People did a test. It was positive for a flu virus at first. But a new test said no. There is no dangerous bird flu here. The area is safe now. People can relax.

4級.title: No Dangerous Bird Flu in Miyagi
4級.text: A dead wild goose was found in Kurihara city, Miyagi prefecture on October 27. A quick test showed a type of bird flu. However, a detailed genetic test found no high pathogenic bird flu virus. The government removed the watching area today. Officials ask people to stay calm and not worry.

3級.title: Bird Flu Test Results Come Back Negative in Miyagi
3級.text: On October 27, a dead wild goose was found in Kurihara City, Miyagi Prefecture. A quick test showed a positive reaction for an avian influenza virus. Because of this, the local area became a special watching zone. However, a detailed genetic test on October 30 proved there was no high pathogenic bird flu virus. Therefore, the Ministry of Environment lifted the special zone. Officials remind citizens that normal hand washing keeps everyone safe today.

準2級.title: Ministry Lifts Special Bird Monitoring Zone After Negative Test
準2級.text: The Ministry of Environment announced that a dead wild goose found in Kurihara City, Miyagi Prefecture, tested negative for high pathogenic avian influenza. The bird was collected on October 27, and an initial rapid test showed a positive reaction for a type of bird flu virus. Consequently, authorities established a special monitoring zone around the location. On October 30, a specialized laboratory conducted a genetic test, which confirmed the absence of the dangerous virus. As a result, the monitoring zone was immediately lifted today. The ministry reminds the public that normal daily hygiene, such as washing hands after touching bird droppings, is enough to prevent infection, and asks everyone to remain calm.

2級.title: Miyagi Bird Flu Monitoring Zone Lifted Following Negative Genetic Test
2級.text: The Japanese Ministry of Environment has officially lifted a special wild bird monitoring zone in Kurihara City, Miyagi Prefecture, after a dead wild goose tested negative for high pathogenic avian influenza. On October 27, local authorities recovered a deceased wild goose and performed a preliminary test that returned a positive reaction for an A-type bird flu virus. In response, officials established a surveillance zone around the recovery site to monitor local wildlife closely. However, subsequent genetic testing conducted by a specialized laboratory at the National Institute for Environmental Studies on October 30 confirmed that no high pathogenic avian influenza virus was present. With the threat ruled out, the monitoring zone was dissolved on the same day. The ministry emphasized that avian influenza rarely infects humans except through intense, direct contact with sick animals. Citizens are urged to maintain calm and practice basic hygiene like handwashing and gargling.

準1級.title: Ministry of Environment Dissolves Miyagi Surveillance Zone After Avian Influenza Test Rules Out Pathogenic Strain
準1級.text: In response to a suspected wildlife health incident, the Japanese Ministry of Environment has officially lifted a specialized wild bird monitoring zone in Kurihara City, Miyagi Prefecture. The sequence of events began on October 27 when officials recovered a deceased wild goose within the municipality. An initial rapid diagnostic test indicated a positive reaction for an A-type avian influenza virus, prompting local authorities to swiftly designate a radius surrounding the recovery site as a special surveillance zone to track potential outbreaks among local bird populations. Nevertheless, subsequent and more rigorous genetic testing performed by a specialized laboratory housed within the National Institute for Environmental Studies yielded definitive results on October 30, confirming the complete absence of any high pathogenic avian influenza virus. Consequently, the government dissolved the monitoring zone the very same day while vowing to continue nationwide wildlife monitoring operations. Emphasizing public safety, the ministry noted that avian influenza transmission to humans is extremely rare under normal daily circumstances, typically requiring intense physical contact with infected animals. Officials have strongly urged the public to remain calm and adhere to standard hygiene practices, such as washing hands and gargling after interacting with nature, while requesting that citizens report any clusters of dead wild birds to local municipal offices.

articles.title: Digital Agency Releases New My Number Card Info Vol. 157 and 158
articles.summaryJa: デジタル庁は民間事業者向けに、マイナンバーカードの活用事例や最新情報をお知らせする「マイナンバーカード・インフォ」のVol.157およびVol.158を掲載しました。また、デジタル認証アプリを「マイナアプリ」に統合したことも発表されています。

5級.title: New My Number Card Info
5級.text: Japan has new news. The Digital Agency has new info for businesses. It is about the My Number Card. Vol. 157 and Vol. 158 are now online. Businesses can read them. They can learn how to use the card. The card helps people every day in Japan.

4級.title: Digital Agency Releases New Info
4級.text: The Digital Agency in Japan released new updates for private businesses and local governments. They published My Number Card Info Vol. 157 and Vol. 158. These volumes share helpful examples of how companies use the My Number Card. Businesses can learn useful ways to check identities and improve their services for customers every day.

3級.title: Digital Agency Shares New My Number Card Info
3級.text: The Digital Agency of Japan has published the latest editions of My Number Card Info, Vol. 157 and Vol. 158. These reports provide private businesses and local governments with helpful examples of how to use the My Number Card. Companies can learn about online identity verification and government policies. Furthermore, the agency recently integrated the digital authentication app into the new Maina App to make services much easier to use.

準2級.title: Japan Digital Agency Releases New My Number Card Information Volumes
準2級.text: The Digital Agency of Japan has published Vol. 157 and Vol. 158 of its My Number Card Info series to help private businesses and local governments. These guides share practical examples of how organizations utilize the My Number Card for identity verification and various administrative services. In addition, the agency recently integrated its digital authentication app into the new Maina App to improve digital services. Consequently, the former digital authentication service has been renamed the Digital Authentication Service, ensuring that administrative bodies and private companies can continue utilizing these secure tools safely for their daily operations across multiple sectors.

2級.title: Digital Agency Publishes My Number Card Info Volumes 157 and 158
2級.text: The Digital Agency of Japan has officially released Volumes 157 and 158 of the My Number Card Info series. These new reports provide private businesses and local governments with the latest updates and helpful utilization examples. Specifically, the publications highlight how various sectors successfully implement the My Number Card for online identity verification and administrative procedures. Meanwhile, the Digital Agency announced that the digital authentication app has been successfully integrated into the newly launched Maina App to improve digital services for users. Because of this integration, the original service has now been officially renamed the Digital Authentication Service. This renaming ensures that administrative organs and private companies can continue to leverage these secure verification tools effectively for their daily operations across multiple sectors. Furthermore, the Digital Agency continues to distribute this useful information regularly to share government policies and card promotion details directly with organizations that need reliable updates for their daily work. These reports help private businesses understand how to use the My Number Card correctly.

準1級.title: Digital Agency Publishes Latest My Number Card Information Volumes 157 and 158
準1級.text: The Digital Agency of Japan has officially published Volumes 157 and 158 of the My Number Card Info series, providing private businesses and local governments with valuable updates and practical utilization examples regarding the My Number Card. These new reports highlight various industry applications. Specifically, Vol. 158 discusses age confirmation using the face-to-face My Number Card application at school festivals, while Vol. 157 features online identity verification using the My Number Card in iPhone applications for loan services provided by NTT Docomo Financial Group, Incorporated. Alongside these published reports, the Digital Agency announced a major structural update regarding its software ecosystem. The features of the former digital authentication app have been integrated into the newly launched Maina App, which began providing services on August 25, 2026. Consequently, the previous digital authentication application service has been officially renamed the Digital Authentication Service. This ensures that administrative bodies, local governments, and private enterprises can seamlessly continue leveraging secure verification tools to enhance their digital services and streamline customer verification procedures across multiple sectors. The Digital Agency of Japan continues to distribute My Number Card Info regularly to share useful information about government policies, card promotion, and practical examples directly with administrative bodies and private business operators who need reliable updates for their daily operations.

articles.title: MEXT Announces New Event for University Students by CS Youth Leaders
articles.summaryJa: 文部科学省は、大学生を対象とした「CSユースリーダーによる大学生対象イベント」の初開催を発表しました。テーマは「地域と学校をつなぐ」であり、若者の地域社会や学校への参画を促進します。

5級.title: New Event by MEXT
5級.text: Japan has a new event. It is for university students. The Ministry of Education makes this event. Young leaders help schools and towns. The event is on December 19, 2026. Students can talk together. It is free to join. Many students can learn new things and help local communities.

4級.title: Event for University Students
4級.text: The Ministry of Education in Japan announced a new event for university students. CS Youth Leaders will hold this event on December 19, 2026, at Yamaguchi University. The main theme is connecting local areas and schools. Students can listen to reports and talk in groups together. This helps young people join community activities easily and learn new things.

3級.title: Connecting Local Areas and Schools
3級.text: Japan's Ministry of Education has announced a new event for university students. Led by CS Youth Leaders, the event focuses on connecting local communities and schools. It will take place on December 19, 2026, at Yamaguchi University. The program includes activity reports from youth leaders, presentations by university students, and group discussions. Organizers hope this will encourage young people to participate in community activities. Admission is completely free, and up to eighty students can join this special gathering.

準2級.title: MEXT and CS Youth Leaders Host Student Event
準2級.text: The Japanese Ministry of Education is promoting youth participation in community schools and local school collaborative activities. To support this goal, they announced a special event for university students organized by CS Youth Leaders. The event theme is connecting local areas and schools through small steps. It is scheduled for December 19, 2026, at Yamaguchi University. The schedule features Ministry explanations, activity reports from youth leaders, student presentations, and group talks. CS Youth Leaders are young people appointed by the Ministry to share the value of community schools through events, speeches, and social media. This free gathering aims to give students an opportunity to get involved in local society.

2級.title: Ministry of Education Promotes Student Community Engagement through New CS Youth Leader Event
2級.text: The Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology in Japan is actively encouraging young generations to participate in community schools and collaborative school activities. As part of this important initiative, the Ministry has announced a newly organized event specifically for university students, hosted by CS Youth Leaders. Scheduled for December 19, 2026, at Yamaguchi University, the event carries the theme of connecting local regions and schools starting from personal interests. CS Youth Leaders are young individuals officially appointed by the Ministry this year to communicate the significance and appeal of community involvement through events, lectures, and social media. The upcoming gathering will feature institutional explanations by the Ministry, activity reports, student presentations, and interactive group discussions among participants. With a capacity of eighty attendees and free admission, the organizers aim to inspire proactive youth participation in regional development and education.

準1級.title: Japan's Ministry of Education Announces CS Youth Leader Initiative Event for University Students to Drive Regional and School Connection
準1級.text: In a continuous effort to promote the integration of community schools and regional school collaborative activities, Japan's Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology has announced a newly planned event specifically tailored for university students. Guided by newly appointed CS Youth Leaders—who are young individuals officially appointed by the Ministry this year to communicate the value and charm of community school initiatives through lectures, event planning, and social media outreach—the upcoming program centers heavily on bridging local communities and educational institutions. Scheduled for December 19, 2026, at Yamaguchi University, the event invites up to eighty undergraduate participants completely free of charge. The comprehensive agenda includes policy explanations from the Ministry, inspiring activity reports delivered directly by CS Youth Leaders, student presentations, and interactive group discussions designed to spark active community involvement. By fostering welcoming spaces where young adults can explore personal connections with local society starting from their own personal interests, the Ministry aims to encourage young generations to participate in community schools and collaborative school activities. The event offers a wonderful opportunity for university students to engage directly with regional development and education. Interested individuals must submit applications through the designated form before December 16, 2026. Through such thoughtful initiatives, Japan's Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology hopes to cultivate a sustainable framework for youth-driven regional revitalization and educational development across the country.

articles.title: Japan Warns Companies About Cyberattacks and Data Leaks
articles.summaryJa: 厚生労働省は、不正アクセスによる個人情報の漏えい事案が相次いでいることを受け、事業者に対してセキュリティ対策の徹底を呼びかけています。

5級.title: Japan Makes New Security Warning
5級.text: Japan has a new security warning. Many computers have bad problems now. Hackers take personal data from companies. The government wants businesses to be safe. You must check your computer systems. Please use good passwords. Keep your data very safe and protected from bad people.

4級.title: New Cyberattack Warnings in Japan
4級.text: Japan is warning companies about cyberattacks. Many computer systems have serious security problems right now. Hackers are stealing personal data from different businesses. The government wants companies to update their systems quickly. Businesses must use multi-factor authentication to stay safe. Leaders need to check their computer safety. Everyone should protect private information carefully today.

3級.title: MHLW Calls for Stronger Cyber Security
3級.text: The Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare is warning companies about security issues. Recently, many businesses suffered cyberattacks and lost personal data from their systems. The government asks all organizations to check their computer security. Companies must apply updates and use multi-factor authentication. Leaders need to make security stronger across their supply chains. Medical organizations must be especially careful with sensitive data and patient information.

準2級.title: Japan Issues Urgent Security Warning After Data Leaks
準2級.text: The Japanese government is urging companies to strengthen cybersecurity measures following recent incidents. Information systems handling large amounts of personal data have been invaded through unauthorized access, and data has been stolen in several cases. The National Cyber Security Operations Office is calling for organizations to take action quickly. This includes applying security patches, handling vulnerabilities through system updates, and strengthening multi-factor authentication. Business leaders must show leadership to ensure these measures are thoroughly implemented across the entire supply chain, including contractors and related partners. Furthermore, the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare reminds medical institutions, healthcare providers, and related companies to check their security measures carefully to prevent further breaches and protect sensitive information.

2級.title: MHLW Urges Strict Cybersecurity Measures Following Data Breaches
2級.text: In response to a series of recent unauthorized access incidents where personal data was stolen from information systems, Japanese authorities have issued an urgent security warning. Large amounts of personal information are handled by businesses whose networks have been successfully invaded by hackers. Consequently, the National Cyber Security Operations Office is calling for immediate action across all sectors. Companies must apply security patches, complete software updates to address vulnerabilities, and strengthen authentication methods like multi-factor authentication. Furthermore, business leaders must show strong leadership to ensure that comprehensive cybersecurity measures are thoroughly implemented across their entire supply chains, including external contractors and partner organizations. The Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare also specifically advises medical institutions, related organizations, and healthcare system providers to review their security guidelines and carefully protect sensitive patient data.

準1級.title: Japanese Authorities Demand Enhanced Cybersecurity Across Supply Chains
準1級.text: Prompted by a concerning wave of unauthorized access incidents resulting in significant data breaches, Japanese authorities have issued a stern nationwide security warning. Hackers have repeatedly infiltrated the information systems of organizations managing vast amounts of personal data, successfully extracting sensitive information. In light of these events, the National Cyber Security Operations Office urges businesses to swiftly implement critical defenses, including security patches, system updates for vulnerability management, and robust multi-factor authentication protocols. Crucially, executives and leadership teams are expected to spearhead comprehensive security enhancements throughout their extended supply chains, encompassing all affiliated contractors and vendors. The Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare has reinforced this message for its jurisdictional sectors, strongly advising medical institutions, related organizations, and healthcare system providers to rigorously review available security guidelines. Organizations are also encouraged to utilize official consultation windows provided by agencies like the Personal Information Protection Commission, JPCERT/CC, and IPA to safeguard their networks against escalating cyber threats, ensuring that patient data and other critical information remain fully protected from unauthorized access at all times across every connected entity in the broader network.

articles.title: The Cursed Cruise: MV Odyssey Passengers Stranded in Cambodia
articles.summaryJa: 永遠の船旅を謳い文句にした豪華客船「MVオデッセイ号」が、燃料費高騰によりカンボジアで突如運航を停止し、乗客が下船を余儀なくされました。

5級.title: The Cruise Ends in Cambodia
5級.text: The MV Odyssey is a cruise ship. Many old people live on it. They want a long trip on the sea. But things go wrong. The ship stops in Cambodia. Passengers must leave the ship fast. They have only seven hours to go.

4級.title: Dream Cruise Becomes a Nightmare
4級.text: The MV Odyssey offered a long trip around the world. Older people paid a lot of money to live on the ship and escape world troubles. They wanted a safe home on the sea for a long time. However, high fuel costs caused very big problems for the company. The price of fuel per cabin went up a lot. Because of this, the company had to stop the cruise. Passengers got a very short notice. They had to leave the ship in Cambodia.

3級.title: The End of the Endless Cruise
3級.text: The MV Odyssey promised passengers a continuous voyage around the world as an escape from political stress and world troubles. People paid large amounts of money for a permanent retirement at sea with many comforts and activities. Unfortunately, an oil shock and rising fuel prices ruined the plan completely. The monthly fuel costs per cabin went up from eighteen hundred dollars to eight thousand dollars. The company abruptly ended the cruise, giving passengers just seven hours to disembark when the ship arrived in Cambodia.

準2級.title: The Cursed Cruise: How a Floating Retirement Ended in Cambodia
準2級.text: The MV Odyssey was designed to offer retirees a continuous voyage around the globe, providing an escape from political anxiety on land. For hundreds of thousands of dollars, passengers enjoyed onboard amenities while traveling the world on a residential cruise. However, global economic pressures and a sharp increase in fuel prices destroyed the business model. Monthly fuel costs per cabin surged dramatically from eighteen hundred dollars to as much as eight thousand dollars, forcing the operating company to cancel the journey. Passengers received a shocking, brief announcement stating they had only seven hours to leave the ship as it terminated its voyage in Cambodia.

2級.title: The Cursed Cruise: The Sudden End of the MV Odyssey's Voyage in Cambodia
2級.text: The MV Odyssey was marketed as an ultimate escape from political turmoil, offering passengers a never-ending retirement at sea with continuous voyages around the globe. For a substantial fee, travelers could embark on a residential cruise complete with food, entertainment, and exotic ports of call. The idea was to give older people a way to cut loose from the troubles of the world. However, the dream of a carefree journey came to an abrupt halt due to severe economic disruptions and an oil shock. A massive spike in fuel prices caused monthly fuel costs per cabin to escalate sharply from eighteen hundred dollars to as much as eight thousand dollars. Unable to sustain these sudden and massive expenses, the operating company abruptly terminated the entire expedition. Passengers were given a stark and brief notice requiring them to disembark within seven hours as the ship docked in Cambodia, cutting their floating retirement short and leaving them unceremoniously dumped in Southeast Asia.

準1級.title: The Cursed Cruise: How the Dream of Endless Luxury at Sea Became a Nightmare in Cambodia
準1級.text: The MV Odyssey was conceived as an ambitious residential cruise designed to offer retirees an uninterrupted voyage around the globe, famously marketed as a way to escape political anxiety on land following Donald Trump's return to the White House. Passengers invested significant fortunes—ranging from hundreds of thousands of dollars upward—to secure cabins for a multi-year journey, anticipating a life of leisure complete with wellness programs, fine dining, a pool, a theater, and exotic destinations. Yet, this floating retirement community ultimately succumbed to harsh global economic realities. An oil shock driven by international conflict triggered a catastrophic surge in operational expenses, with monthly fuel costs per cabin skyrocketing from eighteen hundred dollars to a staggering eight thousand dollars. Overwhelmed by these unsustainable financial pressures, the operating company pulled the plug on the venture entirely. Passengers, many of whom were elderly individuals seeking peace and stability, received a jarring and minimal announcement granting them a mere seven hours to pack their belongings and disembark permanently as the vessel docked in Cambodia, going no further and ending their dream of never-ending luxury at sea.

articles.title: Japan Sports Agency Announces 2026 Sports Town Award Winners
articles.summaryJa: スポーツ庁は「スポまち！表彰2026」の受賞自治体28団体を発表しました。11月17日に東京国際フォーラムで表彰式典が開催されます。

5級.title: Japan Sports Awards
5級.text: The Japan Sports Agency has news. They choose twenty-eight cities and towns for sports. These places work hard for sports and health. A big ceremony is coming on November seventeenth. Many people can meet there. It is in Tokyo. Sports are very good for everyone.

4級.title: Japan Sports Agency Announces 2026 Town Awards
4級.text: The Japan Sports Agency announced the winners of the Sports Town Awards for 2026. Twenty-eight local governments will receive prizes for their great plans to help people enjoy sports and stay healthy. A special ceremony will take place at the Tokyo International Forum in Tokyo on November seventeenth. Many guests will join the important event to celebrate the winning cities and towns.

3級.title: Sports Agency Announces 2026 Town Awards
3級.text: The Japan Sports Agency recently announced twenty-eight winning local governments for the 2026 Sports Town Awards. This program supports communities that create wonderful environments for sports, tourism, and health. Special awards will go to Tottori Prefecture's Nanbu Town and Nagano Prefecture's Urugi Village. An award ceremony will happen at the Tokyo International Forum on November seventeenth, featuring special guests and talks for everyone.

準2級.title: Japan Sports Agency Selects 2026 Local Government Award Winners
準2級.text: The Japan Sports Agency has officially chosen twenty-eight local governments to receive the 2026 Sports Town Awards. Since 2021, this program has supported municipalities that promote sports tourism, disability sports, and healthy community environments. From many creative applications submitted this summer, twenty-eight winners were selected. Special prizes will be given to Nanbu Town in Tottori Prefecture and Urugi Village in Nagano Prefecture. The official award ceremony is scheduled for November seventeenth at the Tokyo International Forum in Tokyo, where sports journalist Akemi Masuda and former rugby star Ayumu Goromaru will also participate as guests.

2級.title: Japan Sports Agency Reveals 2026 Sports Town Award Winners and Ceremony Details
2級.text: The Japan Sports Agency has announced twenty-eight winning local governments for the 2026 Sports Town Awards. Established in 2021 following the Tokyo 2020 Games, this annual program encourages regional municipalities to develop active environments through sports tourism, disability sports experiences, and health initiatives. Following a call for plans launched on July first, judges carefully selected twenty-eight outstanding local governments from across the country based on their enthusiastic ideas. Among the winners, Nanbu Town in Tottori Prefecture earned the Commissioner's Special Award, while Urugi Village in Nagano Prefecture received the Guest Special Award. An official award ceremony will be held on November seventeenth at the Tokyo International Forum. The event will feature Sports Agency Commissioner Junichi Kawai, along with special guest and sports journalist Akemi Masuda, and talk session guest Ayumu Goromaru, a former member of Japan's national rugby team.

準1級.title: Japan Sports Agency Announces Twenty-Eight Municipalities as Winners of the 2026 Sports Town Awards
準1級.text: The Japan Sports Agency has officially revealed the twenty-eight local governments chosen as winners of the 2026 Sports Town Awards. Launched in 2021 following the Tokyo 2020 Games, this annual initiative aims to support municipalities that actively promote sports tourism, disability sports interaction, and healthy community development environments. After receiving numerous enthusiastic ideas following the application period starting last July, twenty-eight regional bodies were selected for their exceptional planning through a careful screening process. Notable winners include Nanbu Town in Tottori Prefecture, which received the Commissioner's Special Award, and Urugi Village in Nagano Prefecture, honored with the Guest Special Award for their distinctive community initiatives. An official award ceremony will take place on November seventeenth at the Tokyo International Forum. The gathering will be attended by Sports Agency Commissioner Junichi Kawai and the winning municipal representatives.
